diagnosis.original_evidence: ID3DXSprite Draw may queue work until Flush or End; StageExtensionEnter originally acquired ScreenHud direct producer owner before isolating a pending previous producer batch. The original direct E8 numeric +TIME path is separate from queued SpriteNodes.
diagnosis.root_cause: At a direct +TIME producer boundary a preexisting homogeneous tracked D3DX batch could be flushed as the first numeric glyph is enqueued, under the incoming ScreenHud scope rather than the outgoing producer. This is a source-proven ownership ordering risk, not yet a hardware-proven cause of observed visual double rendering.
source_trace: hooks_uiscaling.cpp StageExtensionEnter calls FlushD3DXBeforeDirectStageSource before StageExtensionDirectDrawOwner.emplace, preserving original direct E8 callsite logic.

VRProjectedD3DXSpriteIsolationR64::BeforeDirectStageSource checks queue state, live sprite identity and PendingDraws before CanFlushD3DXPreQueueStageBatch verifies old-scope/outgoing producer homogeneity.
The wrapper delegates to FlushTracked(sprite) under the outgoing owner; existing D3DX Draw/Flush/End hooks and queue BeforeQueueNode/BeforeQueueEnd own subsequent per-eye semantics.
alternatives_rejected: Do not flush every D3DX Draw or unconditionally at incoming +TIME glyph entry, because that can relabel other producers and change batching order.
Do not globally classify generic sprites ScreenHud, suppress Lens/SkyGlow, or change game time ticks; they are not bounded by the exact direct stage call.
Do not claim new Quest3 visual correctness from a static mutation guard or passing Windows CI.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: Exact StageExtensionTime producer remains ScreenHud for downstream R26+HUD eye mapping, while preexisting batch is flushed under its saved original owner. Real optical single-image acceptance remains untested.

diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Changed-area verifier rejects omitted direct preflush, ownership acquisition before flush, and forced homogeneous promotion; these are static mutation regressions, not a real D3D/Quest3 execution.
